### **Job Description and Duties**


**Per CCR 249\.3, this job control may be used to fill subsequent vacancies.**  

Under the supervision of the Senior Environmental Scientist (Supervisory), the Environmental Scientist will conduct environmental health inspections of facilities housing egg\-laying hens, calves raised for veal, and breeding pigs to ensure conformance with confinement standards, gather scientific data on food\-animal housing and confinement systems, research and investigate complaints or incidents of farm animal cruelty due to improper housing and care, as well as misbranded products from noncompliant sources, provide analytical expertise and reports on specific livestock confinement parameters on egg\-laying farms, pig breeding facilities, and veal calf production operations, and conduct inspections and audits of distributors, retailers and other end\-users for traceable records of shipments from compliant sources. The Environmental Scientist (ES) will enforce complex environmental health and safety laws and regulations, and execute policies and procedures to improve environmental health, the humane confinement and care of food\-producing animals, and the sustainability of California agriculture.
  

  

As an employee of the California Department of Food \& Agriculture (CDFA), you are required to perform the “essential functions” of the job, with or without reasonable accommodation. If you are interested in becoming part of a diverse and inclusive workforce where talent, experience, and expertise are valued, then CDFA is the place for you!!  

  

  

Be a part of the Animal Care Program team and travel throughout California to ensure Animal Confinement laws and regulations are implemented and enforced.

The duties of this position require the employee to work in the field approximately 70% of the time. This 70% of time includes traveling to locations both inside and outside of California, which includes air travel and overnight travel when necessary. The employee reports to the Sacramento Office, Headquarters Location (at minimum on a quarterly basis), only to pick up supplies, attend meetings and turn in required documents. Travel expenses from the employee’s home to their assigned Headquarters Location are considered a normal commute and are not reimbursable.  

Regular field work involves travel via car throughout California and to various locations across the lower 48 states. Travel for work may include air travel up to three times per month.  

When working in the field the employee may be exposed to extremes in temperatures and high noise levels in a variety of environments ranging from individual farm premises to complex, multi\-story product handling, packaging, and distribution centers. The employee is required to comply with all Departmental Health and Safety Protocols, including the use of appropriate personal protective equipment, participation in required medical clearance, and adherence to safety procedures during field and office duties.

While the CDFA supports telework where possible, in\-person attendance may be required based on operational needs. **Definition**
--------------


**Applications must be filled out** **completely and thoroughly****. Resumes are not accepted in lieu of an application, but may be additionally attached.**

**PLEASE ATTACH ANY DEGREES OR TRANSCRIPTS, LICENSES, AND CERTIFICATIONS TO YOUR APPLICATION.**  

Anchored in the foothills of the Sierra Nevada \- 20 miles east of Sacramento and about 1\.5 hours from Lake Tahoe \- the City of Folsom is comprised of beautiful parks and trails, and boasts excellent schools, family\-orientated neighborhoods, and outstanding shopping, dining, and cultural options. Folsom is a high\-tech, forward\-looking city, with firms ranging from small to large international corporations. Voted by WalletHub as the Best Place for Families to Live in California, and 2nd Best Lake Town in America, Folsom is recognized for its affordability, fair weather, education, and health.  


\-  

The City of Folsom is recruiting for a **Senior Environmental Specialist** to join the **Waste \& Recycling Division in the specialty area of recycling**. This position will focus on recycling compliance programs relating to non\-hazardous materials and will spend a majority of time providing technical assistance, inspections, and enforcement within the community, including program development and record keeping. The ideal candidate enjoys a variety of work environments and tasks, including physical outdoor labor, an office environment, and regular interaction with the public.  

*This is a Monday \- Friday in\-office position, and occasional weekend and after hours work.* *This position is non\-exempt and represented by the Local 39 IUOE union.*  

Under the direction of the **Environmental Specialist Supervisor**, the **Senior Environmental Specialist** performs a variety of operational tasks (program management, educational training, safety awareness, and environmental compliance and audits) related to environmental services in a specialty area (recycling, hazardous waste, air pollution and storm water compliance). Incumbents may oversee, monitor ,and/or direct the work of lower level personnel.

**DISTINGUISHING CHARACTERISTICS**  

The Senior Environmental Specialist is the lead or specialist level in the Environmental Specialist series. In the lead assignment, incumbents provide direction to lower level staff including assigning, directing, and reviewing the work of staff. In the specialist assignment, incumbents work on specialized projects containing a high number of complex, difficult, and sensitive tasks and assignments. Positions at this level are distinguished from those in the lower level classification of Environmental Specialist I/II by the independence with which they perform their duties of handling the more difficult and complex work and performing lead work. This class is distinguished from the class of Environmental Specialist Supervisor in that the latter serves as the supervisor of incumbents in the lower levels of the series and performs the most difficult and complex projects.
**Examples of Essential Duties**
--------------------------------


**NOTE: The following are the duties performed by employees in this classification. However, employees may perform other related duties at an equivalent level. Each individual in the classification does not necessarily perform all the duties listed.**

  

* Assign and monitor the work of lower level staff within the series.
* Develop environmental program designs and operating procedures according to federal and state laws and regulations.
* Provide technical assistance to staff in the development, implementation, and management of residential and commercial recycling programs; edible food recovery; household hazardous waste management programs; and/or storm water and air pollution prevention programs.
* Prepare and submit grant applications and, if awarded, oversee grant implementation and administration, and prepare grant progress reports.
* Assist in the budget development process and administer the respective program's budget.
* Prepare innovative educational and outreach material including flyers, brochures, presentations, displays, news articles, and social media posts.
* Provide information to members of the public, contractors, and consultants regarding hazardous materials, recycling, organics, and food recovery regulations and recycling programs; serve as a resource to city staff regarding proper handling and management of all manners of recyclable materials, organics and food recovery, hazardous and non\-hazardous materials.
* Develop request for proposals for division services, including soliciting suppliers, reviewing proposals, making selection recommendations, and overseeing contracts.
* Compile and analyze data to prepare reports, including state required reports.
* Prepare business correspondence.
* Perform related duties as assigned.

**Employment Standards**
------------------------


**NOTE:** **The level and scope of the following knowledge and abilities are related to duties listed under the "Examples of Essential Duties" section of this specification.**  

  

**Knowledge of:**

* And experience with, composting, including the ability to develop and implement a municipal compost program, and provide educational programs on the subject.
* Methods and procedures used in inspecting, identifying, labeling, packaging, and correcting hazardous conditions associated with hazardous materials or wastes.
* Hazardous material, industrial hygiene, transportation, and disposal practices.
* Principles and practices of emergency preparedness.
* Effects of hazardous materials and their interaction with human health and the environment.
* Recycling techniques as related to the environment, energy conservation, and the economy.
* Laws, codes, regulations, and policies and ability to stay abreast of those that affect the City’s programs.
* Residential municipal, commercial, and industrial waste recycling and disposal programs.

**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description** **AECOM** is seeking an experienced and driven **Client Account Manager \- Air Quality focused** with expertise in air quality compliance (permitting, stack testing, ambient air monitoring) and account management to support business growth and client engagement. This role is ideal for a proven sales leader with an existing book of clients, strong relationship management skills, and a deep understanding of air quality strategies. The selected candidate will be responsible for identifying and securing new business opportunities, driving revenue growth, and delivering innovative environmental solutions.


This hybrid position can be based out of AECOM's offices in Houston, TX; Austin, TX; Chicago, IL; Cincinnati, OH; Denver, CO; Fort Collins, CO; Minneapolis, MN; or Orange, CA. We are also open to candidates not located in these areas, however, must be located within the Western Region of the United States.

**Key Responsibilities include:**

* Develop and execute business strategies to expand AECOM’s air quality compliance services.
* Maintain and grow existing client relationships while identifying new opportunities in the public and private sectors.
* Leverage an existing book of clients to generate sales and secure high\-value environmental projects.
* Work closely with internal teams to develop and present proposals, technical solutions, and service offerings.
* Negotiate contracts and service agreements to align with client needs and financial objectives.
* Provide industry insight and stay updated on air quality regulations, compliance standards, and emerging trends.
* Support cross\-business collaboration to provide integrated environmental solutions across multiple sectors.
* Meet or exceed sales targets while contributing to the long\-term strategic vision of AECOM.

From AUD $110,000\.00 to $119,999\.00 per year**Closing date**
13 September 2026 at 11:55pm
  
***Do you want your work to make a difference for NSW?***  

*Working to protect the state’s environment and heritage.*  

* **Protect NSW's environment through science**
* **Permanent full\-time opportunity, 35 hours per week**
* **Lidcombe office, hybrid working supported**
* **Salary relative to experience, and ranges from $112,375 to $124,158 pa \+ super**

  


Join a passionate team of scientists making a significant impact on environmental protection! Our Science and Insights team is seeking to appoint a Scientist (Ecotoxicology). This is your chance to apply your expertise to important scientific programs and projects and engage in meaningful work that addresses pressing ecotoxicological issues.  

  

**About the role**  

As a Scientist (Ecotoxicology), you will contribute to the design, delivery and analysis of ecotoxicology projects that inform environmental decision\-making and regulation. Working alongside experienced scientists and technical experts, you will support investigations into environmental incidents and research programs, perform ecotoxicity testing, analyse and interpret ecotoxicological data, prepare scientific reports and presentations and collaborate with government agencies, research institutions and other stakeholders to deliver high\-quality environmental outcomes.  

  

The Ecotoxicology team collaborates closely with the Chemical Forensics team, together forming the Environmental Forensics Unit. The role of the Environmental Forensics Unit is to investigate pollution incidents, provide expert advice, and conduct research to protect the New South Wales community, economy and environment from the risk posed by current and legacy environmental contaminants.  

  

This is an exciting opportunity to apply your scientific expertise to real\-world environmental challenges within a collaborative, supportive and knowledge\-driven team. To further strengthen our programs and projects, we provide professional development opportunities and support special interest projects that can enhance the capability and services the Ecotoxicology team provides.  

  

**About You**  

You are a curious and motivated scientist with qualifications and experience in ecotoxicology, including ecotoxicity testing, data analysis and interpretation. You enjoy solving complex environmental problems with scientific rigour and are comfortable working independently or as part of a team. Strong analytical thinking, attention to detail, and effective communication skills will enable you to thrive in this role and contribute to protecting the environment for future generations.  

  

**Essential Requirements**
* Scientific qualifications, knowledge and demonstrated experience in ecotoxicology science including ecotoxicity methods, analysis and interpretation.

  


For more information read the full Role Description: **Scientist (Ecotoxicology)**  

  

**About the Team – Science \& Insights**  

Science \& Insights sits within the **NSW Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW),** which works to protect the state’s environment and heritage while driving a sustainable future for NSW.  

  

Working at the intersection of science, policy and delivery, Science \& Insights collaborates across government, academia, industry and communities to identify priority issues and deliver practical, high\-impact solutions.  

  

The division brings together six specialist branches spanning conservation and restoration, climate and atmospheric science, environmental protection, remote sensing and landscape science, science impact and assessment, and water, wetlands and coastal science.  

  

Together, these teams provide the evidence, expertise and insights needed to understand NSW’s environment, manage risks and drive sustainable outcomes.  

  

The division’s work is focused on building a strong evidence base, advancing innovation in how data is gathered and used, and translating complex scientific information into clear, actionable insights and advice. Through scientific rigour, partnerships and knowledge sharing, Science \& Insights plays a critical role in protecting, restoring and strengthening the resilience of NSW’s environment for future generations.  

  

**Who we are**  

The Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water (DCCEEW) works to protect the state’s environment and heritage. It leads the way on climate change, driving the sustainable transition to a net zero economy, powered by affordable, reliable, and clean energy.  

  

DCCEEW conserves and protects the state’s natural environment. It manages the NSW national park estate, including its rich and diverse biodiversity and Aboriginal cultural heritage for future generations.  

  

DCCEEW also ensures sustainable management of water resources across the state, to support the environment, communities and industry.  

  

We acknowledge the ongoing custodial responsibilities of the Aboriginal peoples of NSW to care for Country and water and are committed to establishing meaningful partnerships with Aboriginal peoples in the management of the environment.  

  

**To Apply**  

If excited by the information above, we look forward to receiving your application, including a copy of your resume (maximum three pages) and cover letter (maximum two page) expressing your interest and suitability for the role.  

  

Please note to be eligible to apply for this position you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or permanent resident, or hold a valid Australian working Visa for the duration of the appointment.  

  

**Applications close 13 September 2026 at 11:55PM.**

Construction Management: for our environmental construction, site remediation, civil construction, and decommissioning projects with a key oil and gas client in the US West Region. Additional project opportunities exist in water (i.e. pumping stations, pipelines, treatment facilities, etc.), transportation (roads, trails, traffic improvements), as well as coastal, environmental, energy. In addition to leading during construction phase, contributions will include involvement in the planning, permitting, design, and procurement phases. This is an excellent opportunity for a qualified Construction Manager to be involved in all aspects of project planning and delivery.
Construction Project Controls: Develop, deliver, and manage budget plans and schedules for construction projects. Monitor and perform budget progress and post-calculations.

Project Development: collaborate with client development team, lead procurement efforts including proposal and interview preparation
Construction Advice: Provide specialist professional advice relating to construction regulations and best practice with regard to constructability, cost evaluations, and sequencing for environmental and civil construction projects.
Knowledge Management: Develop policies and processes, create best practices, set up case studies, and deliver internal knowledge-sharing sessions to capture and share knowledge among colleagues on project/program outcomes and innovative practices in a particular area of expertise and to support the practice.
Personal Capability Building: Act as subject matter expert in an area of construction management and execution for the team. Maintain external accreditations and in-depth understanding of current and emerging external regulation and industry best practices through continuing professional development, attending conferences, and reading specialist media.
Bid Solicitation/Request for Proposal/Tender Analysis: Conduct complex feasibility studies from technological, financial, and organizational perspectives on bid solicitation, including request for proposal (RFP) and request for tender (RFT) project requirements, and review specifications for tenders.
Operational Compliance: Monitor and review performance and behaviors within area of responsibility to identify and resolve noncompliance with the organization's policies and relevant regulatory codes and codes of conduct.

Education

Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree in Civil Engineering, Architecture, Construction Management, or equivalent combination of education and management experience

Experience

Minimum 15 years of experience as Construction Manager and/or Resident Engineer on multiple simultaneous construction projects
CCM certification or Professional Engineer (PE) license a plus, although not required
Experience with web based document management systems

Take on some of the world’s toughest challenges - with everyone at GHD backing you every step of the way.

We'll give you control over your career, empower you to find innovative solutions and help you create a lasting impact.

See where your commitment could take you with GHD.

jobs.title: Hazardous Materials Senior Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

What if you could do the kind of work the world needs?

At WSP, you can access our global scale, contribute to landmark projects and connect with the brightest minds in your field to do the best work of your life. You can embrace your curiosity in a culture that celebrates new ideas and diverse perspectives. You can experience a world of opportunity and the chance to shape a career as unique as you.

The opportunity

As a Senior Consultant in the Hazardous Materials and Occupational Hygiene team, your primary focus is to protect workers' health and provide guidance to clients in order for them to meet their health, safety, and legislative requirements regarding the workplace, and occupational exposure.

This role can be based in our Brisbane or Gold Coast office, and we work hybrid which means you will have the opportunity to work from home 1-2 days per week when not required on site, ensuring a healthy work-life balance.

What You’ll Do

Work within an energetic team environment to maintain a high standard of customer service, technical quality, thriving team culture, and high performance
Develop asbestos monitoring and decontamination strategies, issuing clearances
Conduct sampling for various airborne contaminants such as respirable crystalline silica, dust, and chemicals, as well as physical hazards such as noise and vibration, in order to provide technical recommendations to protect worker health
Undertake site surveys including sampling of suspected hazardous building materials and pre-demolition surveys
Provide technical guidance on sites during asbestos removal projects; and
Conduct indoor air quality, mould and moisture assessments, as well as providing recommendations on the remediation of mould or moisture impacted buildings
Manage a diverse range of small-medium scale projects
Assist the team with strategy and business development
Analyse data and prepare technical reports and proposals with support from senior staff, including technical specialists and Certified Occupational Hygienists (we have 5 of them at WSP!)
We've recently delivered asbestos, HAZMAT, occupational hygiene consultancy services for clients such as: Department of Education, City of Gold Coast, Queensland Health, QBuild, Australia Post, Westpac, Mater Health Services, Urban Utilities, SafeWork Australia, CSIRO, Rio Tinto.

About You

You are enthusiastic, a team player, and looking to make a positive impact in the field of occupational hygiene and hazardous materials consulting by contributing to the safety and well-being of others.

You Will Ideally Bring The Following

Asbestos/HazMat consultancy experience or previous experience in a relevant industry such as environmental management, construction, civil or mining
Experience in measuring and assessing occupational exposure to hazards in the workplace (e.g. environmental factors and stresses, chemical/physical/ergonomic/biological hazards)
Understanding or willingness to develop understanding of consulting and project life cycle, taking initiative to develop relationships with clients, whilst maintaining high standards of service delivery
Appetite to enhance your skills in report writing, building relationships, and project management
Australian Driver's License, enabling you to effectively fulfil the requirements of the position
Trade experience or tertiary qualifications in either Building and Construction, Environmental Science, Health and Safety, Occupational Hygiene or equivalent Asbestos Assessors License would be highly regarded, as it demonstrates your specialised expertise and commitment to maintaining high standards within the industry

Imagine a better future for you and a better future for us all.

Join our close-knit community of talented individuals who share your passion for making a positive impact. Our global team includes more than 69,000 employees, working together to make a difference in communities both close to home and around the world.

An employee Share Purchase Plan is available to all our permanent employees who wish to become owners and vested partners in WSP’s collective success. To find out more about our commitment to the health and wellbeing of our people, and the programs we’ve designed to help you thrive, go to our Employee Benefits page.

With us, you can. Apply today.

jobs.title: Scientist I (GCMS) - Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, LLC - Pomona, CA
jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing  

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.


Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.


With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full\-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

 **Job Description**  

Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, the largest potable water testing laboratory in the US, is searching for a Scientist I in our GCMS department to join our team in Pomona, CA.


This is a full time position, 40 hrs/week.


Duties include:

* Routine sample preparation and analysis of water samples by various written EPA and Standard Methods procedures,
* Performing data process, data entry and written documentation
* Performing routine instrument maintenance.
* Preparation of reagents and standards.
* Other general laboratory related duties as assigned
* Will include regular late shift and/or weekend duties.

  

**Qualifications**  

* Minimum BS degree in chemistry and /or other related science field and one to two years of laboratory experience.
* One to two years of GC or GCMS chemstation experience preferred.
* **Must be available to work overtime including weekends.**
* Excellent math and computer skills
* Excellent written and communication skills
* Excellent attention to details and good organization skills
* Ability to work well independently as well as in a team environment
* Authorization to work in the United States indefinitely without restriction or sponsorship
* Professional working proficiency in English is a requirement, including the ability to read, write and speak in English.

  

**Additional Information**  

This is a full time position Sunday through Thursday 9 am to 5:30 pm with possibility of overtime.


Compensation range is **$22\.20 \-27\.00/ hr (DOE).**

**Candidates within a commutable distance to Pomona, CA are encouraged to apply.**


Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.


As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full\-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

**To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com**

**We support your development!** Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

**We embrace diversity!** Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

**Sustainability matters to us!** At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

**Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/**

 **Eurofins USA Environment Testing is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.**

jobs.description:
At HDR, our employee-owners are fully engaged in creating a welcoming environment where each of us is valued and respected, a place where everyone is empowered to bring their authentic selves and novel ideas to work every day. As we foster a culture of inclusion throughout our company and within our communities, we constantly ask ourselves: What is our impact on the world?

Watch Our Story:' https://www.hdrinc.com/our-story'

We have an exciting opportunity for a visionary Water Resources Management Leader to help shape the future of water resources in the Pacific Northwest and beyond. This is an opportunity for a strategic leader who is passionate about protecting public health, advancing sustainable water solutions, and driving growth across the drinking water, wastewater, recycled water, and stormwater markets. Working alongside local and national leadership, you will play a key role in expanding HDR’s presence, strengthening client partnerships, and delivering impactful projects that support communities for generations to come.

HDR’s Portland Water/Wastewater team is intentionally built differently. Our team combines emerging talent with experienced industry leaders, including several professionals who began their careers at HDR as interns and have grown into leadership roles. We bring together diverse perspectives and backgrounds from across the globe and the Pacific Northwest, creating a collaborative and innovative culture rooted in technical excellence, mentorship, and community impact. Joining HDR Portland means more than taking on a leadership role — it’s an opportunity to help shape a growing practice, influence the future of the industry, and leave a lasting mark on the communities where we live and work.

In this role, you will serve as a trusted advisor and leader for key clients while guiding complex, multi-discipline projects from planning through delivery. You’ll help lead strategic pursuits, identify new opportunities for growth, and collaborate across HDR’s national network of technical experts and business leaders. Projects may include planning studies, design, financial analysis, operations support, alternative delivery, and major infrastructure improvements that directly improve resiliency, sustainability, and quality of life.

We are looking for a leader who thrives at the intersection of strategy, technical excellence, and people development. You will mentor and inspire staff, strengthen HDR’s culture of innovation and collaboration, and help drive continuous improvement across project delivery and technical practices. This role also offers the opportunity to build a visible industry presence through leadership in professional organizations, conferences, and community initiatives.

In the role of Drinking Water & Wastewater Market Sector Leader, we’ll count on you to:

Lead client development efforts and serve as a trusted advisor to key regional clients
Identify and pursue strategic growth opportunities across municipal water markets
Direct and oversee complex, multi-discipline water infrastructure projects
Collaborate across HDR business groups and national practice areas to expand services and capabilities
Promote HDR’s full suite of engineering, planning, and consulting services
Build strong relationships with industry partners, organizations, and senior client leadership
Mentor, recruit, and develop the next generation of water industry leaders
Advance technical excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement initiatives
Support project delivery, QA/QC, risk management, and operational performance
Foster collaboration, knowledge sharing, and work-sharing across teams and regions
Represent HDR through industry organizations, conference presentations, and community leadership activities
Take on impactful project management and leadership assignments that align with HDR’s long-term growth strategy

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in an engineering, planning or a related field
A minimum of 10 years of industry experience
Experienced in development and management of strategic marketing programs for planning and/or engineering services
Experienced in development and management of a wide range of client relationships and specific program and/or project pursuits
Experienced in overall staff development to include recruiting, career path and professional growth
Experienced with industry associations and maintains a visible profile in the market sector
Ability to work cooperatively with Regional Market Sector Directors, Market Sector Directors, Business Class Directors, Regional Business Group Directors, Area Business Group Managers, Area Marketing Managers and Area Managers
Demonstrated commitment to HDR values. An attitude and commitment to being an active participant of our employee-owned culture is a must

What We Believe

HDR is our company. Together, we build on each other's life experiences and perspectives to make great things possible every day. This shapes our collaborative culture, encourages organizational trust and connects us closer to the clients and communities we serve.

Our Commitment

As employee owners, we all have a role in creating an inclusive environment where each of us is welcomed, valued, respected and empowered to bring our authentic selves to work every day.

Our eight Employee Network Groups (Asian Pacific, Black, Hispanic/Latino(a), LGBTQ+, People with Disabilities, Veterans, Women, Young Professionals) help create a sense of belonging and foster a supportive environment where everyone is empowered to engage and contribute. Each group has an executive sponsor and is open to all employees.

jobs.title: Mid-level Environmental Scientist
jobs.description:
**Company Description** **Work with Us. Change the World.**


At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.


There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.


We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description** **AECOM's** **Environment, Health \& Safety team** is seeking an experienced **Mid\-level Environmental Scientist III** to join our team and support and manage environmental compliance programs for public\- and/or private\-sector clients. This mid\-level role is ideal for a candidate with a solid regulatory foundation who can work independently on routine compliance tasks while supporting more complex projects under senior staff guidance. The successful candidate will contribute to technical delivery, client support, and internal collaboration within a consulting\-oriented environment.

**This hybrid position will be based out of our San Jose, CA office.**

**Key Responsibilities include:**

* Environmental Compliance Support.
* Support implementation of environmental compliance programs related to federal, state, and local regulations (e.g., Clean Air Act, Clean Water Act, RCRA, TSCA, EPCRA, and state equivalents).
* Conduct regulatory applicability evaluations, document reviews, and compliance assessments.
* Assist with preparation of permit applications, compliance plans, reports, and regulatory correspondence.
* Support environmental audits and follow\-up corrective actions under direction of senior staff.
* Track regulatory changes and assist with compliance strategy updates.
* Project support \& client interaction.
* Provide day\-to\-day technical support for environmental compliance projects.
* Coordinate with project managers and multidisciplinary teams to meet scope, schedule, and quality requirements.
* Participate in client meetings and site visits as needed.
* Prepare clear, well\-organized technical deliverables and summaries for client review.
* Data Management \& Documentation
* Compile, manage, and analyze environmental compliance data.
* Support development and maintenance of compliance tracking tools and documentation systems.
* Ensure project files and records meet internal quality and compliance standards.

**About AECOM’s Environment Business Line**  

Join AECOM to be part of an expert global team who is connected through a well\-developed, worldwide, internal technical practice network through which you can learn from and brainstorm with the best in the world. AECOM is an industry\-leading, world class environmental firm, and we want you to succeed within it. We respect and encourage your own pathway to excellence via our Freedom to Grow initiative.  

  

AECOM is known for our award\-winning technical excellence, leading\-edge science and innovative project delivery. We provide sustainable solutions for some of the world’s most challenging issues. Our global clients and their projects span a variety of market sectors and geographies and require innovative technical solutions to solve wide\-ranging environmental problems.

 **Qualifications** **Minimum Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, environmental engineering, chemistry, or a related field.
* 4 years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education focusing on environmental compliance within consulting, industry, or a regulatory agency with strong knowledge of key environmental regulations and compliance frameworks.
* Due to the nature of the work, US Citizenship is required.
* Valid Driver's license and motor vehicle records check is required for this role.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Master’s degree or professional certification (e.g., CHMM, CEA) is a plus.
* 6\+ years of relevant experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education focusing on environmental compliance within consulting, industry, or a regulatory agency with strong knowledge of key environmental regulations and compliance frameworks.
* Experience preparing technical reports and supporting environmental permitting or compliance activities.
* Prior experience working in an environmental consulting firm is highly desired.
* Familiarity with state environmental programs and agency interactions.
* Experience with compliance auditing, inspections, or regulatory inspections.
* Proficiency with compliance tracking tools, spreadsheets, or data management systems.
* Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines in a project\-based environment.

  

**Additional Information**  

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. ***To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in\-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.***

 **About AECOM**


AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD\&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well\-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition

Company Description

“The unique culture at AECOM is built on trust, communication, and encouraging consistent growth through unique development opportunities. It’s the combination of open dialogue and transparency that makes me genuinely appreciate working at AECOM.” - Dane Mallinson, Sector Manager GRS

Come grow with us

AECOM's environmental practice is dedicated to helping clients and government to develop critical infrastructure for energy transition, maritime growth, and Defence capability, while protecting the natural environment and meeting their environmental responsibilities. Join our multidisciplinary team providing strategic environmental advice, design optimisation, impact assessment, and management planning to facilitate approvals for the NT’s strong economic growth. Demonstrated experience leading successful application of Commonwealth and State planning and environmental legislation on major projects

jobs.title: Air Quality Managing Consultant
jobs.location: North Sydney, New South Wales, Australia
jobs.description:
Job Description

Position Description

We are seeking an experienced air quality professional to provide technical leadership and project delivery support within Ramboll’s Air and Climate Service Line. This position will focus on complex air dispersion modelling, air quality impact assessment, client advisory services, project management, and mentoring of junior to mid-level colleagues.

The role offers an opportunity to contribute to a growing national air quality practice while working collaboratively across Australian and global teams. Candidates with experience in digital tools, data workflows, automation, GIS, or cross-region technical coordination will be well placed to support ongoing innovation in how air quality services are delivered.

Air Quality Managing Consultant

Working within the Air and Climate Service Line you will be responsible for identifying, conducting and developing air quality projects based on an understanding of business needs, challenges, opportunities and the marketplace. Ramboll is seeking an experienced Air Quality Modelling professional for this position. Our ideal candidate is a technical leader with a proven track record of managing complex, multi-faceted air quality modelling projects, mentoring junior staff, and serving as a trusted advisor to clients. You would be responsible for overseeing project staff and be responsible for project delivery across the air quality team.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Technical Leadership: Lead and deliver complex air quality dispersion modelling and environmental impact assessment projects using regulatory and specialist models such as AERMOD, CALPUFF, CALMET, GRAL/GRAMM, TAPM and WRF. Develop innovative approaches to solving complex air quality, odour, emissions inventory and post-processing challenges.
Project Management: Manage air quality projects, including scope, schedule, budget, resources and quality, to support on-time and on-budget delivery that meets client expectations. Supervise project teams and delegate tasks to junior staff as required.
Technical Review and Quality Assurance: Provide senior-level QA/QC review and technical oversight of modelling analyses, emissions inventories, impact assessments, management plans, approval inputs and technical reports prepared by project teams.
Client and Regulatory Engagement: Act as a trusted client advisor through the full project lifecycle, from early strategy and scoping through approvals, compliance and implementation. Lead or support technical discussions with regulators and approval authorities on behalf of clients.
Staff Mentoring and Development: Mentor junior to mid-level air quality staff by providing technical guidance, training, review and career development support.
Business Development: Contribute technical and business content to proposals, develop scopes of work, support strategic client engagement and identify opportunities for growth in air quality services.
Digital and Cross-Region Collaboration: Support efficient project delivery through digital and technical innovation coordinating with Australian, APAC and global colleagues where specialist input or shared capability is required.

You will be part of the Australian Air and Climate Service Line working within the Air Quality Team as a Managing Consultant. You will lead the delivery of air quality projects, providing technical leadership, project management, and mentoring to junior team members, while supporting the ongoing growth and development of Ramboll’s national air quality capability.

Reporting to the National Air and Climate Practice Lead, you will play a key role in strengthening Ramboll’s air quality services and contributing to the continued success of the team. The position offers the opportunity to collaborate with colleagues across Australia, APAC and our global network to enhance project delivery, provide specialist technical expertise, drive digital innovation and promote technical excellence across Ramboll’s national air quality team.

Qualifications

About You

From the moment you start we will support your personal and professional development so that you can continue to grow with the company. While we look forward to supporting your continued learning and development, for this role we have identified some qualifications, skills and capabilities that will set you up for success:

Bachelor or Post Graduate degree in Environmental Science, Chemistry, Environmental Engineering, Chemical Engineering or related field with minimum 10 years of experience in air dispersion modelling and impact assessment.
Certified Air Quality Professional (CAQP) with the Clean Air Society of Australia and New Zealand and demonstrated involvement in profile raising activities (preferred).
Proficiency in meteorological and air dispersion modelling software such as AERMET, AERMOD, CALMET, CALPUFF, GRAMM, GRAL, TAPM and WRF.
Experience in development of air, odour and GHG emissions inventories across a wide range of industry sectors.
Strong technical knowledge and report writing skills, including preparation of Air Quality Impact Assessments, monitoring reports, Air Quality Management Plans and proposals.
Experienced project management skills, including direct client engagement. Business development skills are highly desirable, as is demonstrated experience in people management and/or mentoring.
Experience in ambient air quality monitoring, stack testing knowledge, climate risk assessment and/or noise monitoring and modelling, is not essential but would be highly regarded.
Experience in the following fields is highly desirable, including GIS software (e.g. ArcGIS Pro and Surfer), programming (e.g. R and Python), and analytical and data visualisation platforms (e.g. MS Power BI).
Excellent communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical, digital or data-related information clearly to clients, regulators and multidisciplinary project teams.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Interesting and diverse projects
The opportunity to work with some of the best and brightest professionals in your field
Flexible work arrangements
Investment in your development
Leaders you can count on, guided by our Leadership Principles
Appreciation for the unique person you are
Inspiration from colleagues, clients, and projects.

We recognise that some candidates only apply when they tick every box. However, passion and potential often outweigh a perfect resume and Ramboll’s supportive learning culture can help you grow. So, if this role resonates with you but you don't meet all the requirements, we encourage you to apply. You might be the perfect fit for this opportunity or another within our team.

Work at the heart of sustainable change with Ramboll

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll employs more than 18,000 people globally across 35 countries. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Buildings, Transport, Water, Environment & Health, Energy, Management Consulting, and Architecture & Landscape. Combining local experience with global knowledge, we help shape the societies of tomorrow.

Equality, Diversity, and Inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion are at the heart of what we do. At Ramboll, we believe that diversity is a strength and that different experiences and perspectives are essential to creating truly sustainable societies. We are committed to providing an inclusive and supportive work environment where everyone is able to flourish and reach their potential. We also know how important it is to achieve the right balance of where, when, and how much you work. At Ramboll, we offer flexibility as part of our positive and inclusive approach to work. We invite applications from candidates of all backgrounds and characteristics. Please let us know if there are any changes, we could make to the application process to make it more comfortable for you. You can contact us at job.advert.accessibility@ramboll.com with such requests.

jobs.title: Scientist I (Metals), Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West, Pomona, CA
jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

Eurofins Scientific is a network of independent companies providing a unique range of analytical testing  

services to clients across multiple industries, to make life and our environment safer, healthier and more sustainable. From the food you eat, to the water you drink, to the medicines you rely on, Eurofins laboratories work to ensure the products they supply are safe, their ingredients are authentic, and labelling is accurate.


Eurofins is dedicated to delivering testing services that contribute to the health and safety of society and the planet, and to its corporate responsibility to protect the environment and ensure diversity, equity, and inclusion across the entire network of Eurofins companies.


With over 50 laboratories and more than 40 service centers nationwide, Eurofins Environment Testing provides full\-service environmental analysis across all 50 states. Our network supports public and private clients—including DoD, DOE, and municipalities—through robust logistics and continuous investment in people, technology, and infrastructure. We offer comprehensive testing for air, water, soil, sediment, tissue, and waste, covering a wide range of analytes including PFAS, metals, VOCs/SVOCs, dioxins/furans, radiochemicals, and more.

 **Job Description**  

 Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West in Pomona, CA is the largest and most recognized water and beverage testing laboratory in the United States, providing water quality compliance and specialty testing to more than 500 municipal, State and Federal customers.


 Eurofins Drinking Water and Wastewater West has a Scientist I opening at our Pomona Laboratory in the Metals department. This is a full time position, 40 hrs/week.


Duties include:

* Routine sample preparation and analysis of water samples by various written EPA and Standard Methods procedures,
* Performing data process, data entry and written documentation
* Performing routine instrument maintenance.
* Preparation of reagents and standards.
* Other general laboratory related duties as assigned
* Will include regular late shift and/or weekend duties.

  

**Qualifications**  

* Minimum BS/BA degree in chemistry and /or other related science field; one to two years of laboratory experience.
* One to two years of ICP\-OES and ICP\-MS (EPA 200\.7/EPA 200\.8\) experience preferred.
* Must be available to work overtime including weekends.
* Excellent math and computer skills
* Excellent written and communication skills
* Excellent attention to details and good organization skills
* Ability to work well independently as well as in a team environmen

  

**Additional Information**  

This is a full time position Tuesday to Saturday 9 am to 6 pm with possibility of overtime.

**Pay Rate Range for this position is** **$22\.20 \- $25 (DOE).**


Candidates within a commutable distance to Pomona, CA are encouraged to apply.


Eurofins Environment Testing (USA) provides a compensation range for informational purposes, the actual base salary may vary based upon, but not limited to, relevant experience and skill set, base salary of internal peers, business sector, and geographic location.


As a Eurofins employee, you will become part of a company that has received national recognition as a great place to work. We offer excellent full\-time benefits including comprehensive medical coverage, life and disability insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays, paid time off, and dental and vision options.

**To learn more about Eurofins, please explore our website www.eurofinsus.com**

**We support your development!** Do you feel you don’t match 100% of the requirements? Don’t hesitate to apply anyway! Eurofins companies are committed to supporting your career development.

**We embrace diversity!** Eurofins network of companies believe in strength and innovation through diversity, being an Equal Opportunity Employer. We prohibit discrimination against employees or applications based on gender identity and/or expression, race, nationality, age, religion, sexual orientation, disability, and everything else that makes employees of Eurofins companies unique.

**Sustainability matters to us!** At Eurofins, we believe sustainability is at the heart of everything we do. Guided by our vision to be the Global Leader in “Testing for Life,” our mission to contribute to a healthier and safer world, and our core values, we are building a strong foundation for Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) initiatives. Eurofins’ commitment to sustainability begins within our own companies through a shared responsibility to people and the planet. With climate change posing an imminent threat, Eurofins and its many companies recognize their duty to proactively reduce or offset the environmental impact of essential operations while also helping our clients do the same—serving as a true ESG Enabler.

**Find out more in our career page: https://careers.eurofins.com/**

 **Eurofins USA Environment Testing is a Disabled and Veteran Equal Employment Opportunity employer.**

jobs.description:
Company Description

This is a Position-Based Test conducted in accordance with CSC Rule 111A.

Application Opening Date: August 25, 2026
Application Filing Deadline: Application filing will be open at least through September 1, 2026 at 11:59PM (PDT), and will close any time thereafter
Location: 505 Paloma Way, Sunol, CA 94586
Recruitment ID: PBT-0922-167137/ RTF0167136-01122585

WHO ARE WE?

San Francisco Public Utilities Commission (SFPUC)

Headquartered in San Francisco, we have 2,300 employees operating across eight counties serving more than 2.7 million customers in the San Francisco Bay Area – 24 hours per day, 365 days per year.

Our Mission
: To provide our customers with high quality, efficient, and reliable water, power, and wastewater services in a manner that values environmental and community interests and sustains the resources entrusted to our care.

Our Vision
: We are an innovative utility leader, recognized for excellent results in service, safety, stewardship, and inclusiveness.

We are an award-winning and industry-leading utilities organization committed to our customers, community interests, and the environment. To learn more about our organization, please visit our website at https://www.sfpuc.org/.

We are proud of our infrastructure and programs, but most importantly, we value our highly qualified and dedicated workforce which ensures that this vision becomes a reality.

To learn more about working at the SFPUC, visit our career site here.

Job Description

About the Natural Resources and Lands Management Division
: The Natural Resources and Lands Management (NRLM) Division within the Water Enterprise of the SFPUC is responsible for the management of approximately 61,000 acres of Bay Area watershed lands under SFPUC ownership as well as 150 miles of utility right-of-way. The NRLM Division is responsible for managing, protecting, restoring, and monitoring the ecological resources on these lands and environmental compliance for the operations and maintenance of the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System which serves 2.7 million customers. We are committed to responsible natural resources management that protects and restores viable populations of native species and maintains the integrity of the ecosystems that support them for current and future generations. We strive to become a leader in science-based and collaborative environmental stewardship in order to continue providing high-quality and reliable drinking water to our customers.

About The Position

The Programs and Operations Manager provides daily oversight, leadership and strategic direction for the Alameda Creek Watershed Center (ACWC), advancing its mission as a hub for public education, community engagement, and watershed stewardship. This position oversees daily operations, including the establishment of clear policies and procedures that support safe, consistent, and high quality operations. The Manager supervises staff and volunteers, fostering a high performing and inclusive team environment. The Manager will be a visible, approachable, and supportive leader who builds trust, develops staff, encourages collaboration, and fosters a positive workplace culture where employees and volunteers can thrive. This position is responsible for overseeing the development of high quality educational and interpretive programs, and ensuring a welcoming and meaningful experience for all visitors. The Manager plays a leadership role in shaping the Center’s public identity, developing partnerships, and leading community engagement efforts that support SFPUC’s mission of service, stewardship, and equity. This position works collaboratively across the Division and the SFPUC on planning and programming efforts that strengthen public understanding of the Alameda Creek Watershed, local ecology, cultural history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System. The role requires initiative, sound judgment, and a commitment to equity, public service, and environmental stewardship.

Work Schedule:
Tuesday through Saturday with occasional work on evenings and Sundays for special events, subject to change if necessary.

Working Relationship:
This position will report to the Alameda Watershed Resources Manager and will supervise a team of staff and volunteers. Initially this position will supervise the ACWC Facility Coordinator and the Education and Volunteers Coordinator, along with 6 part-time staff and several volunteers. This position will require professional, welcoming and friendly interactions with the public and community/agency partners. This position will require collaboration with the facilities team, communications, staff and managers throughout the division, key staff in PUC, including the Assistant General Manager for the Water Enterprise.

Nature of Work:
Portion of the work duties will be outdoors, exposing the incumbent to inclement weather, potential hazards, and animals common in a natural landscape. The position may stand and/or walk for extended periods of time. Ability to work in a busy, noisy environment. Occasionally may lift and/or push 30 pounds of equipment.

Essential duties and responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Strategic Operations and Facility Management

Provide daily oversight of facility operations to ensure a safe, welcoming, and mission aligned visitor experience.
Lead the development and implementation of operational policies and procedures that guide facility use, visitor services, safety practices, and daily operations.
Oversee the aquarium, exhibits, grounds, and community spaces to ensure safe, high quality and consistent standards.
Direct the care, protection, and organization of collections and interpretive materials.
Oversee safety, security, and emergency preparedness efforts in alignment with SFPUC policies and regulatory requirements.
Coordinate maintenance and repairs with the facilities team and contractors, proactively identifying operational needs and improvements.

Interpretation, Education, and Program Leadership

Provide leadership for the development and delivery of interpretive, educational, and public programs that support SFPUC goals and community needs.
Establish interpretive themes related to watershed ecology, cultural and tribal history, and the Hetch Hetchy Regional Water System.
Develop program guidelines, procedures, and quality standards to ensure consistency and excellence across offerings.
Evaluate program effectiveness and develop summary reports using data and community feedback, supporting continuous improvement.
Maintain subject matter expertise in regional natural and cultural history and SFPUC systems.

Community Engagement and Partnership Development

Lead outreach, community engagement, and communications strategies that increase visibility and participation in ACWC programs.
Build and sustain partnerships with public agencies, schools, community based organizations, tribal representatives and local governments.
Represent the ACWC, the Division, and the SFPUC at public meetings, professional conferences, and community events.
Support initiatives that strengthen community relationships, advance equity, and expand access to programs and services.

Staff and Volunteer Leadership

Build and maintain staff capacity to ensure the ACWC is fully and reliably staffed for public operating hours, programs, and special events
Develop staff guidelines, volunteer protocols, and workflow procedures to support consistent operations.
Lead staff development, performance management, scheduling, and training.
Oversee volunteer recruitment, onboarding, training, and engagement programs.
Provide coaching, and support to staff and volunteers, promoting a collaborative, inclusive, and service oriented culture.

Administration and Strategic Planning

Manage budgets, contracts, procurement, and HR related processes in alignment with SFPUC policies.
Develop and maintain administrative policies and procedures that support efficient, compliant, and transparent operations.
Contribute to strategic planning and the development of long term goals, policies, and operational plans for the Division and SFPUC.
Prepare reports and performance metrics that support accountability and continuous improvement.

Ideal Candidate and Competencies:

The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated track record and ability to exercise the following leadership competencies which are critical for success in the role of Alameda and Tuolumne Watershed Resources Manager at SFPUC's Natural Resources & Lands Management Division.

Relationship Management: Builds open, honest, and respectful relationships through effective communication and collaboration techniques. Develops networks and lasting partnerships across boundaries to maintain strategic relationships and achieve common goals. Utilizes a variety of communication approaches to successfully gain support, influence others, and strengthen relationship.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications:
Minimum qualifications reflect the lowest level of acceptable education and/or experience required of an individual such that the individual reasonably could be expected to satisfactorily perform the duties of the position. Candidates must meet all the requirements established by the MQs to be considered for the position.

Education: Possession of a baccalaureate degree from an accredited college or university
Experience: Five (5) years of professional work experience coordinating or directing environmental stewardship, education or related community programs in visitor services, educational programming, interpretive center operations, or community engagement; Experience managing budgets, contracts, or administrative processes and collaborating with community partners, public agencies, educators, or local governments.
License: Possession of a valid and current California driver’s license.

Substitution:
Additional qualifying professional experience may substitute for the education requirement on a year for year basis for up to 2 years. One (1) year is equivalent to thirty (30) semester units/forty-five (45) quarter units.

Note: One year of full-time employment is equivalent to 2000 hours. (2000 hours of qualifying work experience is based on a 40-hour work week.)

Applicants must meet the minimum qualification requirement by the final filing date unless otherwise noted. Applicants who meet the minimum qualifications are not guaranteed to advance through all of the steps in the selection process.

Desirable Qualifications:

The stated desirable qualifications may be used to identify job finalists at the end of the selection process when candidates are referred for hiring.

Supervisory experience with staff and volunteers interacting with the public.
Experience developing or implementing policies, procedures, or standard operating guidelines for community, non-profit or public facilities, such as visitor centers or education centers.
Experience supporting operations for a community facility (opening/closing, safety procedures, coordinating maintenance and repairs).
Experience representing and working within a public agency or large governmental or nonprofit organization, such as a park agency, public utility or municipal government.
Leadership experience in supporting interpretive centers or environmental education programs.
Experience developing interpretive exhibits, educational materials, or public programs.
Knowledge of California natural and cultural history, ideally focused on the Diablo Range and Bay Area, including the regional geography, plants and animals.
Experience in community engagement and outreach.
Knowledge of and experience working with local tribes.
Experience collaborating with regional Bay Area community and environmental organizations.
Experience managing contracts.
Experience building partnerships with diverse communities and supporting equitable access to public services.

At Apex, we’re building more than a consulting and engineering firm—we’re creating a place where your career accelerates, your contributions matter, and your potential is fully realized. Our success is grounded in strong leadership, a collaborative culture, and a shared commitment to delivering exceptional outcomes.

As we continue to expand, we're looking for high-performing professionals who are ready to lead, collaborate, innovate, and create impact. At Apex, you help shape what's next. When we succeed together, we share in that success. All Apex positions are eligible for annual bonus opportunities, reinforcing our commitment to recognizing and rewarding meaningful contributions that drive our collective growth.

Environmental Scientist/Industrial Hygienist

Locations: Los Angeles or Orange County | ~50% field / 50% remote

Apex is seeking an environmental professional with experience in industrial hygiene to perform asbestos, lead-paint, mold/moisture intrusion, exposure assessment, abatement monitoring, and related industrial hygiene and EHS compliance projects across Southern California.

Employee Benefits

This role offers competitive compensation and a robust benefits package, a balanced mix of fieldwork and report writing, company sponsorship for professional and vocational training, work from home opportunity, collaboration with other industrial hygiene, EHS and other experts, and continued professional development and growth afforded by a rapidly growing national environmental consulting company.

Key Responsibilities

Perform asbestos, lead-based paint (LBP), and microbial/moisture intrusion assessments, along with abatement oversight, with an approximate 50/50 split between field and office work
Conduct safety and compliance assessments in accordance with regulatory standards and client requirements
Support additional environmental services through cross-training, including:
Exposure assessments
Workplace safety evaluations
Stormwater compliance inspections
Soil and groundwater sampling
Noise and air monitoring
Aboveground Storage Tank (AST) inspections

Execute work in alignment with project work plans, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and direction from project managers
Manage scheduling and logistics across all project phases, from coordination and fieldwork through reporting
Prepare clear, accurate, and technically sound client-ready reports using project-specific templates
Collaborate with internal teams to support project delivery and ongoing professional development
Maintain and proactively pursue relevant certifications, including 40-Hour HAZWOPER, CAC, and/or CSST

Qualifications

2+ years of professional experience conducting asbestos surveys and mold/moisture intrusion inspections as an AHERA-accredited inspector (in any state)
Current AHERA certification required
California Certified Asbestos Consultant (CAC) and/or Certified Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) preferred
Bachelor’s degree in Environmental Science, Industrial Hygiene, Microbiology, or a related field

What We’re Looking For

Self-motivated and dependable professional who can work effectively with limited supervision
Strong technical writing and critical thinking skills
Solid analytical and math skills for interpreting laboratory data and preparing reports
Excellent attention to detail with the ability to manage multiple projects and deadlines
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to collaborate in a team-oriented environment
Physically capable of performing fieldwork and comfortable working in both field and office settings
Commitment to safety and a strong understanding of safe work practices
Interest in growing within industrial hygiene and expanding into broader environmental consulting services

Why You'll Love Working For Us

Company-subsidized medical and dental.
Company-paid life, short, and long-term disability.
401k match, tuition assistance, and more.
Cross-training and the ability to work on a variety of projects.
Performance-based bonuses or other incentives.
Working with the best and brightest in the industry.
2,000+ employee national firm with 70+ locations across the US.

1155 Coleman Avenue, San Jose, CA 95110

Job description:

About the Company:

Founded in 2006, we are a leading provider of global employment outsourcing solutions that empower businesses with top talents recruitment, cost optimization, ensure compliance, and streamline hiring processes abroad.
With global operations spanning the AP, EMA, LA and NA, ZONBERATION has served over 30 Fortune 500 companies and leading internet corporations across diverse industries, including automotive, e-commerce, tech products, consumer goods, gaming, real estate and finance.

Position Summary:

Our company maintains long-term, stable partnerships with many international corporations. Our work with leading technology companies continues to grow. We have successfully integrated top-tier professionals directly into their operational teams, enhancing their capabilities across multiple functions and contributing to shared success.
We are now recruiting a dedicated and detail-oriented Senior EHS Specialist to join our client’s dynamic tech environment. In this specialist role, you will be responsible for executing comprehensive EHS strategies, maintaining compliance, conducting risk assessments, and supporting the development of a strong safety mindset across all venues, including corporate offices, production facilities, and major events.

Job Description / Scope Of Work
Job Title:
Senior EHS Specialist
Location:
San Jose
Job Type:
Full-time
Job Overview

We are seeking an experienced and proactive Senior EHS Specialist to join our team. This role will be responsible for driving the implementation of EHS strategies, ensuring business operations comply with corporate policies and local regulations, fostering a strong safety culture, and enhancing employee health and safety awareness.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership:
Develop, implement, and continuously improve regional EHS strategies, policies, and procedures in alignment with corporate and business objectives.
Compliance & Risk Management:
Ensure full compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local EHS regulations. Proactively identify, assess, and mitigate EHS risks across operations.
Incident Management:
Lead and oversee incident response, investigation, root cause analysis, and corrective action implementation to prevent recurrence.
Auditing & Inspection:
Plan and conduct regular EHS audits, inspections, and assessments. Track and drive closure of action items to ensure sustained compliance and safety performance.
Program Development & Training:
Design, deliver, and maintain effective EHS programs, training, and communication initiatives for employees at all levels.
Stakeholder Collaboration:
Work closely with cross-functional (XFN) teams—including Operations, HR, Facilities, and Legal—to integrate EHS into business processes and promote initiatives such as wellness, ergonomics, and employee assistance programs.
Reporting & Analysis:
